- Model consistently overestimates prices in early forecast windows, especially after recent spikes; apply downward bias correction for first 5–7 days of forecast horizon.
- After a price spike (e.g., >45.0), model tends to overshoot and fail to correct downward; reduce forecast slope by 10–15% in subsequent days.
- When sentiment history is flat (all 0.00), model exhibits high variance and overconfidence; apply smoothing filter or reduce forecast volatility by 20–30%.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon; if forecast is >40.0 for 3+ consecutive days, adjust downward by 1–2 points per day until convergence to recent 10-day average.
- If true outcome shows sharp drop after spike (e.g., 48.22 → 42.19), model fails to anticipate rapid decline; add early warning buffer (e.g., 3–5 day lagged drop) to next forecast.
- Forecast horizon 30d is prone to “tail risk” overfitting; if recent 10-day average is below 40.0, cap forecast at 40.0–41.0 to avoid overcorrection.
